components.name: Featured Choice Card
components.description: A service to connect on the welcome screen: white logo plate, name, plain detail, arrow; the beacon lights on hover or focus.
components.css: .ds-card { display:flex; align-items:flex-start; gap:16px; min-height:112px; box-sizing:border-box; padding:30px 20px; border-radius:12px; background:#FFFFFF; border:1px solid #C5CBC3; font-family:Inter, 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; color:#29332E; cursor:pointer; text-align:left; width:320px; transition:background 150ms, border-color 150ms; } .ds-card:hover { background:#EBF0EC; border-color:#3F6654; } .ds-card:active { background:#DEE6DF; } .ds-card:focus-visible { outline:none; border-color:#92581D; box-shadow:0 0 0 2px #92581D; } .ds-plate { position:relative; flex:none; width:52px; height:52px; border-radius:14px; background:#FFFFFF; border:1px solid #D6DBD4; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; } .ds-beacon { position:absolute; top:-3px; right:-3px; width:7px; height:7px; border-radius:50%; background:#FF9D32; border:1px solid #EBF0EC; opacity:0; transition:opacity 150ms; } .ds-card:hover .ds-beacon, .ds-card:focus-visible .ds-beacon { opacity:1; } .ds-text { flex:1; display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:2px; margin-top:5px; } .ds-name { font-size:16px; line-height:22px; font-weight:600; } .ds-detail { font-size:13px; line-height:18px; color:#4B564D; } .ds-arrow { flex:none; height:52px; display:flex; align-items:center; color:#4B564D; } .ds-card:hover .ds-arrow, .ds-card:focus-visible .ds-arrow { color:#3F6654; }

components.name: Horizon Banner
components.description: Welcome-only brand band: photograph on midnight, a left midnight shade, ivory serif headline. The photo is replaced here by a midnight-to-slate gradient.
components.html:
A calmer place for your mail.
Welcome to Overlook. Connect an account to bring your mail in.
components.css: .ds-banner { position:relative; height:240px; background:linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(16,28,36,0.95) 0%, rgba(16,28,36,0.6) 68%), linear-gradient(180deg, #2A4656 0%, #101C24 100%); display:flex; align-items:center; padding:0 32px; overflow:hidden; } .ds-banner-inner { display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:12px; } .ds-display { font:400 48px/56px 'Source Serif 4 Display', Georgia, serif; color:#F0EBDD; max-width:640px; } .ds-lead { font:400 15px/22px Inter, 'Noto Sans', sans-serif; color:rgba(240,235,221,0.84); max-width:520px; } @keyframes ds-veil { from { opacity:0.6 } to { opacity:0 } } .ds-banner::after { content:''; position:absolute; inset:0; background:#101C24; opacity:0; animation:ds-veil 1400ms cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); pointer-events:none; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-banner::after { animation:none; } }

narrative.northStar: A Clear View of What Matters
narrative.overview:
Overlook translates an alpine overlook into a working mail client: a place to pause and see the landscape clearly. The system is two registers kept firmly apart. The working interface (mail lists, reading pane, settings, dialogs, the welcome's choices) is neutral, spacious and literal: Inter on theme surfaces, pine or glacier-blue for action, flat cards on tonal grounds. The brand register (the horizon mark, the serif wordmark, the alpine-dawn photograph, a single amber beacon) appears only at edges of the experience: title-bar lockup, welcome, About, launch materials. Mail content always outweighs branding.

Density is Outlook-familiar: a three-pane workspace, 12 to 13 px Inter for metadata and lists, generous reading surfaces that stay white in every light colorway. Seven colorways (Light "Soft stone", Dark, Gray, Blue, White, Alexander, Pink, plus Follow system, which can adopt an Omarchy desktop palette) all share one icon set, one layout, one type hierarchy and one set of status colors; only color changes. The palettes are centralized in `crates/overlook-app/src/theme.rs` and tested for contrast; no screen invents its own palette.

Confirmed rejections, from the brand system: no bright neon, fantasy mountains, oversized moons, orange sunset washes or camping insignia; no landscape behind working mail; no amber body text on pale grounds; no wilderness puns or jokes about overlooking mail.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral-first: roughly 85% surfaces and text, 10% slate/pine and selection, at most 5% warm accent.
Two type voices: Source Serif 4 Display for brand moments, Inter for everything that works.
Flat tonal layering at rest; shadows only for floating elevation.
The beacon: one small amber light, never a fill colour for controls.
Every interactive element has a visible keyboard focus state in the theme's focus colour.

rules.name: The Beacon Rule
rules.body: Beacon amber is a small light, not a fill. It may appear as the mark's beacon or as a dot of a few pixels that lights on hover or focus. Never use it as a button fill, body text, or a wash.

rules.name: The One Palette Source Rule
rules.body: Every app colour comes from `Palette` in `theme.rs`, or is derived from it with a stated mix (as the welcome's card tones are). Brand constants (Midnight, Ivory, Beacon) are painted only on brand material: the tile, the mark, the photograph.

rules.name: The White Paper Rule
rules.body: Every light colorway keeps a white message centre; email content renders on white paper with `#20242B` ink regardless of the shell theme. Sender colours always win.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 Display appears only in brand moments (wordmark, welcome, About, marketing), never in mailbox rows, forms or dialogs. Inter carries everything else.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings and labels are plain sentence case in Inter; there are no uppercase labels above headings. The one native exception is the calendar's weekday column headers (11px uppercase day abbreviations), which are data labels, not decoration.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards on a page carry no shadow; they lift by fill and a 1px edge. If a ground and its cards are too close in luminance (the white-surface colorways), step the ground toward the frame or ink rather than adding a shadow.

rules.name: The Unshadowed Mark Rule
rules.body: The horizon mark and app icon are never given shadows in the product.

dos: Do take every colour from `Palette` and test new foreground/background pairs for 4.5:1 (3:1 for focus and control boundaries), as `theme.rs` does.
Do keep the message centre white in every light colorway and email on white paper.
Do put a midnight shade under any words set on the photograph.
Do give every custom interactive element a keyboard focus state in the theme's focus colour, and an accessible name.
Do show third-party sign-in marks unaltered, on white plates, with provenance recorded in `branding/providers/README.md`.
Do keep feedback transitions brief (120 to 180 ms); reserve longer motion for a single brand moment such as the welcome veil.
donts: Don't use Beacon amber (#FF9D32) as a control fill, body text or wash; it is a small light.
Don't set amber body text on a pale background.
Don't use Source Serif 4 Display in mailbox rows, forms or dialogs.
Don't place the alpine landscape behind working mail; it belongs to onboarding, landing and launch surfaces.
Don't add shadows to cards at rest or to the horizon mark.
Don't invent screen-specific palettes or user-defined custom colours.
